clue.text: Searched for somewhere to spend the night

parts.note: pro is Latin-derived for 'in favour of', i.e. for
a bed is where one sleeps the night

explanation.surface: Someone hunted around for a place to stay overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to investigate closely, so a past-tense search fits.

clue.text: Salesman revises orders, being dictatorial

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: putting the letters into a new order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A salesman rewrites his purchase orders in an overbearing way.
explanation.definitionFit: A repressive regime crushes dissent, a quality of dictatorial rule.

clue.text: Gamble on a foreign character

parts.note: to gamble is to bet

explanation.surface: Placing a wager on someone from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign character.

clue.text: At end of play they do this sketch on puzzles

definitions.text: At end of play they do this

parts.note: to sketch is to draw
to stump someone is to baffle them

explanation.surface: At the close of the game, people doodle over their brainteasers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bat-and-ball game, 'stumps' are the wooden posts; umpires remove them to end a day's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket officials signal the close of a day's play by pulling up the wooden posts.

clue.text: Set loose in Paris, one parts heading north

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards

explanation.surface: In Paris, someone splits up and travels north.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstrap something is to unfasten its straps, setting it free.

clue.text: Having no end of attractiveness, one cleans up

indicators.note: lacking its final letter, so the last letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: charm is attractiveness

explanation.surface: Endlessly charming, someone tidies up after others.
explanation.definitionFit: A char, or charwoman, is a British term for a cleaner employed in homes or offices.

clue.text: Security pass on the side

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
lateral means relating to the side

explanation.surface: A security pass is worn at one's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged as security for a loan.

clue.text: Risk fortune

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hazard; as a noun it means luck or fate.

clue.text: Exhaust resources in practice session

definitions.meaning: to ... money is to spend it all quickly
a rehearsal of a show from start to finish

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the phrase: squandering funds, and a full rehearsal before the real performance.

clue.text: Mole's holiday by river?

parts.note: a short holiday is a break
a river is a body of water

explanation.surface: A small burrowing animal takes a vacation beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is a red herring: a mole is also a stone pier or sea wall. Read 'Mole's' as 'Mole is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole in the harbour sense is a massive stone wall protecting an anchorage from waves.

clue.text: New regulation ahead for fine linen

indicators.note: the regulation piece goes in front of the new piece

parts.note: a regulation is a law

explanation.surface: A fresh rule has been brought in concerning quality linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn is a fine, sheer cotton or linen fabric named after the French town Laon.

clue.text: Nurse regularly meeting journalist, which is enjoyed

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word nurse

parts.note: ED is the usual crossword shorthand for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A nurse often meets a reporter, which she likes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enjoyed in the sense of had or made use of, as in 'enjoyed the facilities'.

clue.text: Deeply agitated, first to get wrapped up in breeze

indicators.note: one piece is enclosed by the breeze word

parts.note: a draught is a current of air
1st, written IST in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone becomes very upset before bundling up against a cold wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraught means extremely worried and upset, i.e. deeply agitated.

clue.text: Sort of verb taken from passage, I have to conclude

indicators.note: the contraction for 'I have' comes at the end of the word

parts.note: transit is passage from one place to another
contracted, I have becomes I've

explanation.surface: A grammarian explains a verb category drawn from a reading passage.
explanation.definitionFit: A transitive verb is a grammatical kind that takes a direct object.

clue.text: Superficial understanding shown by second of concern?

parts.note: something that is mattering is of concern

explanation.surface: A shallow grasp is revealed by a brief worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight, surface-level knowledge of a subject.

clue.text: Folly one's revealed in fancy plumbing fixture

parts.note: vanity in the sense of futility or folly
a unit is one, read as 'one is'

explanation.surface: Self-regard comes to light in an elaborate bathroom fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A vanity unit is a washbasin set into a cupboard, a bathroom fixture.

clue.text: Secure part that's appealing

parts.note: to secure a prize is to win it
some is a part of the whole

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a component that looks attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome describes charming, attractive qualities, a synonym for appealing.

clue.text: Guarantee to get organised after conflict, with time

indicators.note: the organised piece follows the conflict piece

parts.note: war is armed conflict
to run an event is to organise it, so ran

explanation.surface: Pledging to arrange things once fighting ends, given enough time.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrant is an assurance or authorisation, close in sense to a guarantee.

clue.text: Crowd round honey-maker welcoming Spaniards' positive reaction, for example

indicators.note: the bee takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a bee makes honey
si is Spanish for yes

explanation.surface: A bee surrounded by Spaniards responds to their enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To besiege is to surround a place with forces, crowding around it.

clue.text: Free port erects a position to examine one's past

definitions.text: a position to examine one's past

indicators.note: letters freed from their order are rearranged

explanation.surface: A free port puts up a building for viewing history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges PORT ERECTS. The definition points to the phrase 'in retrospect', looking back from the present.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is the standpoint of looking back over past events.

clue.text: Band's award

definitions.meaning: a rosette or ... given as a prize or honour

explanation.definitionFit: A narrow strip of material, and a medal ribbon given in honour.

clue.text: Successive notes delayed

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
te follows la in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Musical notes played one after another arrive behind time.
explanation.definitionFit: Late means coming after the expected time, a synonym for delayed.

clue.text: Lover to live with a Unionist

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
U is an abbreviation for Unionist in UK politics

explanation.surface: A romantic partner moves in with a Unionist politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or admirer, an old-fashioned word for a male sweetheart.

clue.text: Drink up

parts.note: a toast taken by a rider already mounted, i.e. up in the saddle

explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a farewell drink offered to someone on horseback about to leave.

clue.text: Stitched four ways

parts.note: south is one of the four compass points
east is another compass point
west is a third compass point
north completes the four compass points

explanation.surface: Something sewn in four different directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn is the past participle of sew, meaning stitched.

clue.text: Little being put together for each one

parts.note: per means for each
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A small creature is assembled piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy-like being in Persian mythology, a small sprite.

clue.text: Dry goods will be carried here?

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means teetotal; read literally it is where cargo rides on a cart.

clue.text: Dodgy legality when two learners go merrymaking

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate letter, so two give LL

explanation.surface: A dubious legal matter when two novice drivers head off to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when two learners go' removes LL from LEGALITY; 'Dodgy' rearranges the remaining EGAITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaiety is lively celebration and festivity, which is merrymaking.
